feature: The scope bar: Enterprise, organization, team, project, feature; every project page sits under it
An organization's page and a team's page: their projects, the models they use, spend and value, no person of their own; an organization asks for a domain model through a consulting session
A project in ten tabs: Overview, Plan, Features, Connect, Traces, Operations, Quality, Self-healing and training, Increments, Members
A feature's page in eight tabs: Overview, Models and flow, Prompts, Quality and thresholds, Evaluation set, Feedback, Increments, Settings
A model's page in eight tabs: Overview, Improvement, Usage, Adoption, Cost avoided, TL Index, Built from, Training
A feature is held to two kinds of bar: ThinkLatent's threshold on the TL Index and the team's own range on its own measures
No roles: members give support, the owner decides, with ThinkLatent's two people on each project
The Plan: five phases, five parties with named leads, what each owes and the lead times, open to everyone from the first day
Requests and their status: four kinds of request on one page
Traces in five views with Sessions folded in, every field the trace store keeps, and a switch that seals text
Self-healing and training in a project: requirements, gaps, readiness to train, no training data shown; projects do not train
A new version offered to a project with its results already run; an old version stays 90 days
Cost avoided in five layers, on a model and on the Value page; layer 2 waits for one real consulting proposal
Help: ask, ask an expert, problems in the open, answered before; Ask Jarvis with three kinds of answer, handed to a person when needed
Leaderboards by kind beside the TL Index: speech, decision and the rest, ours beside outside models
Connect: no keys anywhere; applications registered outside the portal sign in through Okta; one endpoint per feature; a sample call with feedback and outcome calls; limits only on shared endpoints
A project's open view for everyone, with its numbers and features; a restricted project shows only its name, team and contact
A team can offer its own agent for the shelf; ThinkLatent scores it and the team stays its owner
Alerts fire only from what is agreed or from a change the SRE agent sees; the Enterprise's incident tool keeps the record
Five things can start an increment, a smaller model among them; every rollout starts with a silent day and moves by itself
Operations across the Enterprise: every endpoint, the machines, what the next six weeks need; training machines as a total only
The record inside each project: six kinds of line, auditors through a read-only role, an export that expires, kept for the project's life and then by the Enterprise's rule
Every item in the store carries seven tags: what it can train, pillar, category, source and rights, sensitivity, who checked it, shape; pipelines set them and people check them
A knowledge graph of the tags selects from disk; a mix is a question put to the graph, with its checks
LM safety and cyber attack data are open to the whole foundation team, and every mix shows its share
Only the foundation team sees the Data and Training pages; rows are read only on a review or a data set's page, and every opening is recorded
Recipes built in the portal from 22 methods: standard ones defined at the start, new ones from the methods available; starting a run freezes its recipe
Shape the base first in every base recipe (adjust, prune by width, distil back); trials at 5, 10 and 20% judged against 2 points allowed on any live pillar
One run with its stages inside; a failed check stops it for a person; best and last checkpoints kept; the portal proposes and the lead decides
A run's storage: a readable run id, four places, pointers not copies, 180 days, and the record travels with a released model
After a run: the whole TL Index confirms it, it is released, projects are told and their evaluations run, each project decides
Reuse only from a released item or a passed stage of a run still kept; a base shelf for the foundation team
The training stack: AutoModel, NeMo RL and Gym, Curator, DataDesigner, Evaluator and Model Optimizer, with Skills and Run considered; no Megatron-Bridge; Gemma and Phi bases
A prompt's text lives in the application and is registered with each version; the project's members and its two ThinkLatent people read it
A system of models has one catalogue page with its own score and thresholds; the models inside show to ThinkLatent only, or also to the project that built it
Everyone sees a model's size class and cost per request; parameter count and machine cost show to ThinkLatent only
Registering the application is the project's engineers' step on the Plan, with AI engineering as help
A new edition every two weeks: 100 questions in and 100 out at random, corrections with it, signed by the Head of ThinkLatent
At each edition only new and corrected questions are scored and the overall score is a delta; outside models get a full run each month and at once on a change
A stage-check set of 1,200 questions for checks inside training, never in an edition; a question keeps its side
Only the Index team reads TL Index questions; the people who train models see scores and question ids
A dedicated Index team keeps the Index fresh and makes every correction
A training run's check shows nameless in the open evaluation queue
At most 5 real calls among a pillar's 20 incoming questions an edition, so outside models can still be scored
Notifications stay inside the portal: no email, no chat
A 'What is coming' page in Help carries later-year features by year, with a small 'Planned' line where each will live
Try TLM: LibreChat underneath, every screen in the ThinkLatent look and built from the kit, every LibreChat feature on day one, a button at the top of every page
